newsitem.title: NORWAY: POLL-Analysts upgrade EPS estimates on PGS.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Analysts upgrade EPS estimates on PGS.

text.p: Analysts said on Thursday they had upgraded earnings estimates for Norwegian offshore services and seismic company Petroleum Geo-Services ASA (PGS) after the company booked record profits for the first half of 1997.
Of five Norwegian analysts polled by Reuters, four said they recommended a buy on the stock, while one had a negative opinion.
On Wedneday PGS shares jumped 36 crowns, or 10 percent, to 406 crowns after the company reported a 53 percent surge in pre-tax profits in the first half from a year ago to $38.59 million.
At 1300 GMT on Thursday, the stock was two crowns down at 404 crowns.
For estimates of earnings per share (EPS) for 1998, the analysts upgrade forecasts by an average 2.9 percent.
"The outlook is good. The seismic market continues to be extremely tight," said one analyst. "The new capacity that is arriving in the market is not sufficient to cover the increase in demand."
Average estimates for 1997 EPS were adjusted to $2.11 per share from $2.03 and for 1998 to $2.81 from $2.73. For 1999, EPS was upgraded to $3.62 from $3.52.
Most analysts were agreed, however, that there was a risk tied to the share.
"The growth that they (PGS) plan will be expensive," commented one.

The more negative analyst with a sell recommendation said: "They cannot remain technologically superior for ever. It (the share) was at a high price before and yesterday's 10 percent rise was definitely an over-reaction."
Another analyst said he projected a 50 percent rise in PGS' share price in the next two years.
